$comment: Narwhal's Money Tips. text is shown to everyone; advanced adds detail in Advanced mode. topic links to the Learn menu.

tips.text: Pay yourself first: put some money in savings before you spend.
tips.advanced: Automate it, a fixed % of every paycheck to savings means you never 'forget'.

tips.text: Needs come before wants. Food and a home first, then the fun stuff!
tips.advanced: Many 'needs' have a 'want' version (water vs. fancy soda). Spot the upgrade.

tips.text: Interest earns interest. That's compound interest, and it grows like a snowball!
tips.advanced: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt). More time beats a higher rate more often than you'd think.

tips.text: Money growing at 8% a year doubles in about 9 years.
tips.advanced: Rule of 72: years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate%. Works for debt too, 24% APR doubles in 3 years!

tips.text: Keep an emergency fund for surprises like a broken bike.
tips.advanced: Aim for 3–6 months of expenses in a safe, easy-to-reach savings account.

tips.text: Bigger isn't always cheaper. Compare the price per item!
tips.advanced: Unit price = price ÷ quantity. Stores count on you not doing the math.

tips.text: Want something? Wait a day. If you still want it tomorrow, think again.
tips.advanced: The 24-hour rule beats impulse buys. For big purchases, try 30 days.

tips.text: Don't put all your eggs in one basket. Own lots of different companies.
tips.advanced: Diversification lowers risk without lowering expected return much. Index funds do it for you.

tips.text: An index fund is a basket with a tiny piece of many companies.
tips.advanced: Low-cost index funds beat most professional stock pickers over 15+ years, after fees.

tips.text: Paying back only a little at a time can take years and cost a lot!
tips.advanced: Paying only the minimum on a $3,000 card at 25% APR can take over 10 years.

tips.text: Borrow less than you can, and always pay on time.
tips.advanced: Keep credit-card utilization under 30% (under 10% is even better) to protect your score.

tips.text: If a message says 'hurry!' and asks for passwords, it's probably a scam.
tips.advanced: Urgency + secrecy + unusual payment (gift cards, crypto) = classic scam pattern.

tips.text: Never share passwords or your PIN, even with a friend.
tips.advanced: Banks never ask for your full password or PIN by text or email.

tips.text: Your paycheck can be smaller than your pay because of taxes.
tips.advanced: Gross pay − taxes − deductions = net pay. Budget with net, not gross.

tips.text: Taxes help pay for roads, parks and schools.
tips.advanced: A raise never lowers your take-home pay: only the dollars in the higher bracket pay the higher rate.

tips.text: Starting to save early gives your money more time to grow.
tips.advanced: $100/month from 16 to 65 at 7% beats $300/month from 40 to 65.

tips.text: Some jobs add free money to your savings if you save too!
tips.advanced: An employer match is an instant 50–100% return. Always contribute enough to get it.

tips.text: Prices slowly go up over time. That's called inflation.
tips.advanced: Real return = (1 + nominal)/(1 + inflation) − 1. Cash under the mattress loses value.

tips.text: When you choose one thing, you give up the other. That's the trade-off!
tips.advanced: Opportunity cost is the value of the best option you didn't choose.

tips.text: Profit is the money left after paying for everything.
tips.advanced: Profit margin = profit ÷ revenue. High revenue with thin margins can still lose money.

tips.text: A business has to sell enough to cover its costs before it makes money.
tips.advanced: Break-even units = fixed costs ÷ (price − variable cost per unit).

tips.text: When lots of people want something rare, the price goes up.
tips.advanced: Elastic goods: small price changes cause big changes in quantity demanded.

tips.text: A budget is a plan for your money before you spend it.
tips.advanced: 50/30/20: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings & debt payoff (after taxes).

tips.text: Write down what you spend. Small things add up!
tips.advanced: A $5 daily habit is $1,825 a year. Track for one month to find leaks.

tips.text: Insurance helps pay when something big goes wrong.
tips.advanced: Higher deductible = lower premium. Choose a deductible you could pay from your emergency fund.

tips.text: Banks pay you interest for saving and charge interest when you borrow.
tips.advanced: APY includes compounding; APR usually doesn't. Compare savings by APY and loans by APR.

tips.text: A bond is like an IOU: you lend money and get paid back with interest.
tips.advanced: When interest rates rise, existing bond prices fall (and vice versa).

tips.text: A company's stock price goes up and down. Think long term!
tips.advanced: P/E = price ÷ earnings per share. A high P/E means investors expect fast growth.

tips.text: If something promises to make you rich super fast, be careful!
tips.advanced: Chasing hype usually means buying high. Guaranteed high returns are a red flag for fraud.

tips.text: Investing a little bit every month is a great habit.
tips.advanced: Dollar-cost averaging buys more shares when prices are low and fewer when high.

tips.text: Sharing some of your money can help your whole community.
tips.advanced: Check a charity's overhead and reports. Legit charities are transparent.

tips.text: New cars lose value as soon as you drive them away.
tips.advanced: A new car can lose 15–20% of its value in year one. Used cars depreciate slower.

tips.text: Renting and buying a home each have good and bad sides.
tips.advanced: Buying usually wins only if you stay long enough to cover closing costs and maintenance.

tips.text: Saving for a big down payment makes a home cheaper in the long run.
tips.advanced: 20% down avoids mortgage insurance and lowers your monthly payment and total interest.

tips.text: Being trustworthy with money helps you borrow for cheaper later.
tips.advanced: A 100-point better score can save tens of thousands in interest on a mortgage.

tips.text: A quarter is 25 cents. Four quarters make one dollar!
tips.advanced: Making change: count up from the price to the amount paid.

tips.text: Give your savings a goal, like a bike. It's easier to save for something!
tips.advanced: SMART goals: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound.

tips.text: Working is how most people earn money. Get better and you get paid more!
tips.advanced: Skills + experience = higher pay. Negotiating your first salary compounds for decades.

tips.text: You can earn money by helping neighbors: walking dogs, washing cars, raking leaves.
tips.advanced: Freelance income usually has no tax withheld, set some aside for taxes.

tips.text: Only shop on websites a grown-up says are safe.
tips.advanced: Look for the real domain, HTTPS, and reviews from outside the site before buying.

tips.text: Paying bills on time saves money. Late fees are no fun!
tips.advanced: Late payments stay on credit reports for years. Autopay at least the minimum.

tips.text: Got more money? Save some of the extra, not just spend it!
tips.advanced: Avoid lifestyle creep: when income rises, raise your savings rate first.

tips.text: Small fees can eat a lot of your money over time.
tips.advanced: A 1% yearly fee can take about a quarter of your ending balance over 30 years.

tips.text: A business needs cash to pay bills, even if it's making sales.
tips.advanced: Profitable businesses still fail from bad cash flow: money in must arrive before money out.

tips.text: Different countries use different money. You trade one for another.
tips.advanced: Exchange booths profit from the spread between buy and sell rates, plus fees.

tips.text: Fun spending is okay! Just plan for it so you don't run out.
tips.advanced: Budget for wants on purpose. Guilt-free spending is part of a healthy plan.
